sections.title: 英语知识运用
sections.directions: Directions: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

blocks.content: Here's a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you're the CEO of a small business, and though you're making a nice

growth by establishing a growth team. A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus
on finding ways to grow. Let's look at a real-world

departments of engineering, marketing and product development. This brought them good results until 2012, when their growth plateaued. The

questions.analysis: profit 【线索】「生意做得不错却要更上一层」的小企业语境 线索在本句的后半句 you need to find a way to take it to the next level——「需要更上 主语 you're the CEO of a small business，能让 CEO 描述「做得不错」的，自然是赚钱多 【选项】A) purchase ✗ 对象错——CEO 「做」的不是采购 purchase 意为「采购、购买」，是公司花钱的动作，与 making a nice __ 这种「做出好成果」的 B) profit ✓ 搭配地道且语义贴合 profit 意为「利润」，make a profit 是固定搭配，正好对应小企业 CEO 「赚得不错」的状态， 与下文 take it to the next level 形成「赚得不错→想做更大」的语义递进。 C) connection ✗ 话题偏离——下文没接「人脉」 D) bet ✗ 感情色彩冲突 【验证】代入后整句为 you're making a nice __(1)__ = 「你赚着一份不错的利润」，与紧接其后的 you need to find a way to take it to the next level「但需要更上一层楼」逻辑顺承，也

prioritize 【线索】全段在号召把增长放在第一位 线索在空后的 by establishing a growth team——专门组建团队来做这件事，等于把增长 摆到突出位置；再加上 it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus __(3)__ on 【选项】A) define ✗ 动作错位——不是「定义」是「去做」 define 意为「定义、界定」，是认知动作；作者要的是行动，与 establishing a growth team 这 B) predict ✗ 方向错——不是预测，是推动 predict 「预测」也是认知层面的，没法解释为什么要 establishing a growth team；且全文是讲 C) prioritize ✓ 完美契合「专设团队聚焦增长」 了 What you need to do 的「具体动作」。 D) appreciate ✗ 色彩与对象都不对 【验证】代入后整句为「你需要做的是把增长放在第一位，办法是组建一支成长团队」，与紧接的 focus __(3)__ on finding ways to grow 形成「优先→专注」的同向加强。

exclusively 【线索】团队的全部精力都给增长 线索在同一句 A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus __(3)__ on finding ways to grow——专门攒一个团队做这件事，意味着精力是「只放在增长上」 而不是「暂时」「也许」「起初」。再回望第 2 题的 prioritize，本句正是 prioritize 的展 【选项】 A) exclusively ✓ 把 focus 推到「只」的极致 exclusively 意为「专一地、唯一地」，与 focus on 搭配地道，正好表达「全部精力只放在找增 长之道上」，呼应上句的 prioritize。 B) temporarily ✗ 时间限定与「专门组队」相悖 temporarily 「暂时地」会把整个团队矮化为临时安排，与 prioritize、establishing a growth C) potentially ✗ 语气太虚——不是「可能」 D) initially ✗ 暗含「后来不再」与下文不符 【验证】代入后为「团队靠协作的力量，专一地聚焦于寻找增长之道」，对内承接 prioritize、对外

example 【线索】下面是 BitTorrent 的故事而非实验或辩论 线索在紧接的 Prior to forming a growth team, the software company BitTorrent had 50 employees working in the __(5)__ departments of engineering, marketing and product development——下文直接讲一家真实公司的经历，没有「实验设计」「正反方 【选项】A) experiment ✗ 下文不是实验设计 B) proposal ✗ 下文不是提议 C) debate ✗ 下文没有正反观点 D) example ✓ 正是「举一个真实案例」 example 「例子」与下文「举出 BitTorrent 这家公司」精准匹配，且 a real-world example 在 【验证】代入后整句是「我们来看一个真实世界的例子」，与下文 BitTorrent 案例自然衔接，也呼应 了 overview 中「案例佐证」这一段的功能。

traditional 【线索】「成立成长团队前」的常规架构 线索在同句状语 Prior to forming a growth team 与全文对比框架：前文 A growth team is made up of members from different departments 把成长团队定义为「跨部门」的新 做法；那么「之前」自然指的是公司沿用已久的、按 engineering/marketing/product development 分立的「老套」结构。 【选项】A) identical ✗ 事实错——三个部门并不相同 identical 「完全相同的」明显与 engineering、marketing、product development 三种不同部 B) marginal ✗ 色彩冲突——这些是核心部门 C) provisional ✗ 时态错——不是临时设置 provisional 「临时的、暂定的」与 Prior to forming a growth team 暗含的「长期常规架构」 D) traditional ✓ 对「新做法」之前的「老套」精准对照 traditional 「传统的、老套的」正好与下文 growth team 这一「新做法」形成对照，也契合 BitTorrent 案例「旧架构走到瓶颈」的故事走向。 【验证】代入后「BitTorrent 在传统的工程、营销和产品研发部门里有 50 名员工」与紧接的 This brought them good results until 2012, when their growth plateaued 形成「传统架构

problem 【线索】增长停滞 + 顾客不付费=问题 线索一在上句 until 2012, when their growth plateaued——增长停滞本身就是负面状 态；线索二在本句 that 从句 too many customers were using the basic, free version of their product 与下句 few people were making the upgrade——这描述的是一个「不付 【选项】A) rumor ✗ 事实非「未经证实」 B) secret ✗ 并非隐秘信息 C) myth ✗ 并非「广为流传的错误观念」 D) problem ✓ 完美匹配「困境」语境 problem 「问题」直接对接上句 their growth plateaued 的负面状态，把「免费用户太多、付 【验证】代入后整段叙事变成「2012 年增长停滞 → 问题是太多人用免费版 → 故事接着要找答 案」，与第 3 段 Things changed... when ... 的「找到解决之道」节拍严丝合缝。

despite 【线索】「付费版有改进」却「升级的人少」是让步 线索一是空后的 improvements to the premium, paid version——付费版有改进，是正 面事实；线索二是主句 few people were making the upgrade——结果却很少有人升 【选项】 A) despite ✓ 正反差让步关系一拍即合 customers were simply unaware of the premium version 给出的真因配套。 B) unlike ✗ 对比对象错位 unlike 「不像、与…不同」要求空后是被对比的事物，而 improvements 不是用来与「升级少」相 C) through ✗ 方式与结果矛盾 D) besides ✗ 并列增量与反差结果不搭 【验证】代入后整句变成「尽管付费版有所改进，却很少人愿意升级」，与下段提出的真因「客户其

however 【线索】上段是困境、本段是转机 线索一在 P2 末 few people were making the upgrade——困境停滞；线索二在本句 Things changed 与同句的 an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard 【选项】A) moreover ✗ 并非追加同向信息 moreover 「此外」表同向追加，但 P3 是与 P2 反向的转折，方向相反。 B) however ✓ 上段困境到本段转机正需 however C) therefore ✗ 并非因果直接推出 therefore 「因此」要求 P2 是直接原因、P3 是必然结果；但 P2 没有任何「自动导致变化」的逻 D) again ✗ 无重复语境 【验证】代入后段首读作「然而，事情发生了变化——一位富有创意的项目营销经理加入」，与 P2

created 【线索】P2 公司还没有成长团队 线索在 P2 开头 Prior to forming a growth team——明确点出此前没有成长团队；那 存在）。 【选项】A) inspected ✗ 无可检查的既有团队 B) created ✓ 从无到有的「组建」 created 「创建」精准对应「BitTorrent 此前没有成长团队，新人来后才组建」的事实，呼应 P1 的 establishing a growth team。 C) expanded ✗ 扩张需有原物 D) reformed ✗ 改革也要有原物 【验证】代入后整句为「一位富有创意的项目营销经理加入，创建了一支成长团队，激发出他们所需 的新视角」，把 P1 的方案（成立成长团队）与 P3 的故事节点（创建发生在 BitTorrent）

fresh 【线索】「创新经理」+「跨部门视角」=新视角 线索一是同段 an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard 里的 innovative；线索二是紧接的解释句 By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the __(11)__ of upgrades wasn't due to a quality 视角」。 【选项】A) cultural ✗ 话题外延偏离 B) objective ✗ 侧重「客观」与上下文不符 C) fresh ✓ 与 innovative、跨部门视角共振 fresh 「新鲜的、新颖的」与同段 innovative、跨部门换视角的描述高度共振，「fresh perspective」更是英语中固定说法。 D) personal ✗ 色彩与团队属性矛盾 【验证】代入后整句为「他激发出了他们所需的那种新鲜视角」，下句正好接上「从营销视角看工程

lack 【线索】上一段「很少人升级」 = 升级少 线索一是 P2 末 few people were making the upgrade——少有人升级，本质是「缺乏升 级」；线索二是本句下文 Most customers were simply unaware of the premium 【选项】A) end ✗ 事实错——升级并未终结 B) burden ✗ 色彩错——升级不是负担 C) lack ✓ 对应「升级很少」的本质 lack 「缺乏」直接对应 few people were making the upgrade 的事实，且下文「客户不知道 D) decrease ✗ 走向错——文中没说在下降 同 decrease。 【验证】代入后整句为「升级的缺乏并非源于质量问题」，下文紧接「真正原因是大多数客户不知道

insight 【线索】P3 末「发现真因」=洞察 线索是 P3 末整句 By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the __(11)__ of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue. Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version and what it offered——这是 【选项】A) policy ✗ 上文未给出政策 B) suggestion ✗ 上文非「建议」 C) purpose ✗ 目的与上文事实错位 D) insight ✓ 正是上段「发现」的同义提升 insight 「洞见、深入理解」精准对应上段「换视角发现真因」这一认知收获；armed with this insight 是英语中常见说法。 【验证】代入后整句为「带着这条洞见，营销和工程团队联合起来…」，下文 raise awareness by prominently __(13)__ the premium version 正是「洞见 → 行动」的自然落地。

promoting 【线索】「提升认知」需要「推介/推广」型动作 upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent——升级量暴涨、收入大 【选项】A) contributing ✗ 搭配错——contribute to 后才接名词 contributing 「贡献」常用 contribute to，直接接 the premium version 搭配不通；语义上也不 B) allocating ✗ 动作对象错 allocating 「分配、分派」常用于资源分配（allocate funds），而这里要的是「让用户认识到付 C) promoting ✓ 「推广」精准对接「提升认知」 promoting 「推广、推介」与 raise awareness 是同向同步动作，下句的「升级暴涨」也是推广 D) transferring ✗ 对象错——不是「转让」 【验证】代入后整句为「通过把付费版突出地推介给免费版用户来提高认知度」，下句 upgrades

As a result 【线索】上文「推广」=因，「升级暴涨」=果 线索是上句 raise awareness by prominently __(13)__ the premium version to users of the free version——主动推广是原因；本句 upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent 是结果。一因一果，标准的「因此/结果」关系。 【选项】 A) As a result ✓ 因果关系精准对应 B) At any rate ✗ 语气与因果链不符 C) By the way ✗ 话题切换错——这里不是岔话 D) In a sense ✗ 限定语气不对 【验证】代入后整句变成「于是，升级量暴涨，收入增长了 92%」，与上段「推广动作」形成清晰

unite 【线索】「跨学科团队 + 让大家走在轨道上」=凝聚 线索一是空后宾语 the interdisciplinary team——「跨学科」意味着成员来自不同部门、 需要被「拧成一股绳」；线索二是并列动作 keep them on course for improvement—— 【选项】 A) unite ✓ 「凝聚跨学科团队」是核心动作 unite 「使联合、凝聚」正好回应 interdisciplinary 这一「多元成员」属性，并与 keep them on course 形成「先聚再带」的连续动作。 B) finance ✗ 话题错——leader 角色不是出钱 finance 「资助、出资」是 CFO 类角色的事，与 leader 的「带队」角色错位。 C) follow ✗ 主客倒置 follow 「跟随」会让 leader 反过来跟随团队，与下文「leader 要确定目标区域」的主导地位 D) choose ✗ 范围错——不是「挑选」 【验证】代入后整句为「需要一个能凝聚这支跨学科团队并使其保持改进方向的人」，与下句 This leader will __(16)__ the target area, set clear goals 中「leader 确定目标」的主导动作形

identify 【线索】「设定目标前」要先「确定目标区域」 线索是同句并列动作 set clear goals 与 establish a time frame——这两步发生前必须先 【选项】A) share ✗ 动作错位——不是「分享」目标区 share 「分享」会变成「leader 把目标区域分享给别人」，但此处是 leader 主导决策动作，不是 B) identify ✓ 「确定目标区域」是首要动作 identify 「确定、识别」与 target area 是地道搭配：identify the target area「确定目标区 域」是先于 set goals 的标准步骤。 C) divide ✗ 动作错——不是切分 D) broaden ✗ 方向错——不是扩大 broaden 「扩大、拓宽」与下句 keeping the team focused 的「聚焦」相反，会冲淡 target 的 【验证】代入后整句为「这位 leader 将确定目标区域，设定明确目标，并为完成这些目标制定时间

accomplishment 【线索】目标是用来「完成」的 线索一是 set clear goals 与 establish a time frame——设目标定时限，对象只能是「实 现目标」；线索二是下段 keeping the team focused on moving forward——团队要不 【选项】A) announcement ✗ 动作错——不是宣布 announcement 「宣布」是一瞬间的动作，无需 time frame；并且 set clear goals 后接「宣布目 B) assessment ✗ 对象错——评估不是目标的终点 assessment 「评估」是后续动作，但 time frame for 通常指向一个核心结果，而目标的核心结果 C) adjustment ✗ 前提错——目标不是用来调整的 D) accomplishment ✓ 「完成目标」是 time frame 的天然对象 P6 的 moving forward 同向。 【验证】代入后整句为「为完成这些目标制定时间表」，set goals → time frame for accomplishment 是项目管理通用三步走，全文行文连贯。

responsible 【线索】句中 keeping ... 是 leader 的具体职责 线索是 keeping the team focused on moving forward and steering them clear of distractions——这是非常具体的 leader 职责清单；上句 keep them on course for improvement 也已经在交代 leader 的职责。故 be ___ for 是「负责…」之意。 【选项】A) famous ✗ 语义错位 famous for 「因…出名」会变成「leader 因为带队聚焦而出名」，话题与上下文「岗位职责」 B) responsible ✓ 「负责…」精准对接职责陈述 responsible for 「负责…」与「带队聚焦、避免分心」这类岗位职责描述无缝匹配。 C) available ✗ 状态错 available for 「可被…使用」让 leader 变成「资源」，与他主导团队的角色不符。 D) respectable ✗ 属性错——不是评价 respectable 「值得尊敬的」是评价性形容词，与 for + V-ing 也不构成自然搭配；语义不对。 【验证】代入后整句为「该 leader 还负责让团队保持聚焦、避开干扰」，与下句的「干扰识别」自 然连贯，整段「leader 职责」主题清晰。

While 【线索】「吸引力 + 分心」一正一反 = 让步 线索是同句两半 attractive, new ideas 与 can be distracting——「虽然有吸引力但可能让 人分心」是典型让步；再看下句 must recognize when these ideas don't __(20)__ the 【选项】A) Before ✗ 时间关系不对 B) Once ✗ 条件结果错 C) While ✓ 让步连词最契合「虽诱人却可能分心」 D) Unless ✗ 否定条件错 【验证】代入后整句为「虽然新颖诱人的想法可能让人分心；团队领导者必须识别…」，与紧接的 must recognize 形成「让步铺垫 → 行动要求」的标准教学语气。

serve 【线索】「服务于目标」才不该被搁置 线索一是同句 need to be put on the back burner——若想法不能服务于目标就该搁置； 线索二是上段反复强调 keep them on course for improvement、keeping the team focused on moving forward——团队要紧扣目标。两条线索都指向「服务目标 = 留；不 服务 = 搁置」。 【选项】 A) serve ✓ 「服务于目标」是地道搭配 serve 「服务于、有助于」与 the goal 搭配地道（serve the goal），完美对接「不服务目标就 B) limit ✗ 方向错 C) summarize ✗ 对象错 summarize 「概括、总结」搭配 a goal 不通顺，「不概括目标 → 搁置」的因果也不成立。 D) alter ✗ 方向错 【验证】代入后整句为「当这些想法不服务于当前目标，需要被搁置时…」，与上文「leader 让团队 OVERVIEW · 通读建境 门成员构成的成长团队（growth team），并以 BitTorrent 的真实案例佐证其有效性，最后 落到对成长团队领导者的要求。开篇即定调：you're the CEO of a small business, and though you're making a nice __(1)__, you need to find a way to take it to the next level，提 出 establishing a growth team 作为解。 P1 抛出 CEO 痛点并给出方案——组建成长团队（What you need to do is __(2)__ growth by establishing a growth team）；P2-P4 用 BitTorrent 案例走完「问题→洞察→见效」闭 环：先是 their growth plateaued，再到 Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version 的洞察，最后 upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent；P5-P6 转向团队领导者，强调他要 keep them on course for improvement 并 keeping the team focused on moving forward。识别出这三段走向，是逐空判断逻辑词、 SENTENCE INSIGHTS · 句子精讲 11 Here's a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you're the CEO of a small business, and though you're making a nice profit, you need to find a way to take it to the next level. sections.title: 阅读理解
sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

blocks.content: In the quest for the perfect lawn, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut—and it is the environment that is paying the price. About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles. The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year's event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos. The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity. Ed Home, of the RHS, said: "We launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic. We recommend using real grass because of its environmental benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment." The RHS's decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problems fake grass causes. A Twitter account, which claims to "cut through the greenwash" of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers. It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an "ecological damage" tax on such lawns. They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures. However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol. The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more. The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend an average of £500 on trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects. In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has "no plans to ban the use of artificial grass". It added: "We prefer to help people and organisations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters. However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives."

It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park? But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling. But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service. Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life. The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks. The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life. The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system —an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in

The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer ("an ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain," for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders. In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but "adapting to new communications technology," Sparrow says. In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as "cognitive offloading." Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance. Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside. Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet. "I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things," Sparrow says, adding that we haven't lost our ability to do it. Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains. There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles. "There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I'd have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs," observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. "It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don't know."

Teenagers are paradoxical. That's a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language. But the paradox is scientific as well as personal. In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other. At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers. A new study published in the journal Child Development, by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand. The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence. For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved. The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk. The researchers studied "prosocial" and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old. The participants filled out questionnaires about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend, or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late. Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older. But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior. Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly helping a friend. Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness. The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others. The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together. Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments? One idea is that teenage behavior is related to what researchers call "reward sensitivity." Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs. "Reward sensitivity" measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk. Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you. Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age. Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn't seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.

sections.directions: Part B Directions:Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column. There are two extra choices in the right column. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

blocks.content: Net-Zero Rules Set to Send Cost of New Homes and Extensions Soaring New building regulations aimed at improving energy efficiency are set to increase the price of new homes, as well as those of extensions and loft conversions on existing ones. The rules, which came into effect on Wednesday in England, are part of government plans to reduce the UK's carbon emissions to net zero by 2050. They set new standards for ventilation, energy efficiency and heating, and state that new residential buildings must have charging points for electric vehicles. The moves are the most significant change to building regulations in years, and industry experts say they will inevitably lead to higher prices at a time when a shortage of materials and high labour costs are already driving up bills. Brian Berry, chief executive of the Federation of Master Builders, says the measures will require new materials, testing methods, products and systems to be installed. "All this comes at an increased cost during a time when prices are already sky high. Inevitably, consumers will have to pay more," he says. Gareth Belsham, of surveyors Naismiths, says people who are upgrading, or extending their home, will be directly affected. "The biggest changes relate to heating and insulation," he explains. "There are new rules concerning the amount of glazing used in extensions, and any new windows or doors must be highly insulated." Windows and doors will have to adhere to higher standards, while there are new limits on the amount of glazing you can have to reduce unwanted heat from the sun. Thomas Goodman, of MyJobQuote, says this will bring in new restrictions for extensions. "Glazing on windows, doors and roof lights must cover no more than 25% of the floor area to prevent heat loss," he says. As the rules came into effect last Wednesday, property developers were rushing to file plans just before the deadline. Any plans submitted before that date are considered to be under the previous rules, and can go ahead as long as work starts before 15 June next year. Builders which have costed projects, but have not filed the paperwork, may need to go back and submit fresh estimates, says Marcus Jefford of Build Aviator. Materials prices are already up 25% in the last two years. How much overall prices will increase as a result of the rule changes is not clear. "Whilst admirable in their intentions, they will add to the cost of housebuilding at a time when many already feel that they are priced out of homeownership," says Jonathan Rolande of the National Association of Property Buyers. "An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs." John Kelly, a construction lawyer at Freeths law firm, believes prices will eventually come down. But not in the immediate future. "As the marketplace adapts to the new requirements, and the technologies that support them, the scaling up of these technologies will eventually bring costs down, but in the short term, we will all have to pay the price of the necessary transition," he says. However, the long-term effects of the changes will be more comfortable and energy-efficient homes, adds Andrew Mellor, of PRP architects. "Homeowners will probably recoup that cost over time in energy bill savings. It will obviously be very volatile at the moment, but they will have that benefit over time." matter.
